title: How to Make a Simple Video for Your Small Business Using Biteable
author: Tom Sliker
excerpt: I am always looking for new ways to tell a story or communicate a message, and there is no doubt that video is a good way to do that.
html:
I am always looking for new ways to tell a story or communicate a message, and there is no doubt that video is a good way to do that.

One of my clients, a regional multi-campus tech school, recently told me that they are using a service called Biteable to make short explanation videos.  You can see my first effort below.

Of course, Broadstreet Consulting is a subscriber to Adobe's Creative Cloud software, which includes Adobe Premiere Pro, and we do have the skills to make videos with that, but I thought I would take a look at this light-weight Web-based offering.

I decided to test it out, and within just a few minutes I had put together something very simple from one of their templates. Of course, I can easily enhance this by loading my own images and my own videos, and a better clearer message, but for about 10-15 minutes effort I thought this is a really nice and simple tool for getting the message out quickly with no video editing skills required.

Biteable is free if you are okay with the Biteable.com watermarks on your video, and just $99/year if you'd like to remove the watermarks. A very good deal if you asked me.

Tom S.

Broadstreet Consulting on Biteable.
